rrc-wells.reasoning: The only probed source that is first-party (the regulator itself), free, unauthenticated, and verified statewide by four-corner probe (Panhandle 10, East TX 222, Permian 568, South TX 215) with a full-Texas extent of -106.93..-93.15 lon / 25.73..36.51 lat and 1,396,049 features. It is a strict superset of the Harris mirror both spatially (mirror returns 0 in the Permian where this returns 568) and attributively: it adds GIS_SYMBOL_DESCRIPTION (54 distinct human-readable status strings), GIS_LOCATION_SOURCE (positional provenance), GIS_WELL_NUMBER and GIS_API5, none of which the mirror carries. Migration is not a re-point of the same shape: the mirror's SURFACE_ID/WELLID/LONG83/LAT83 become UNIQID/GIS_LONG83/GIS_LAT83, so fetch-wells.ts parseWellFeature must be remapped. Orphan status should come from joining layer 2 (11,937 features) on API rather than being inferred, which is what deriveOrphanedFlag currently does from SYMNUM.

rrc-pipelines.reasoning: First-party RRC T-4 permit alignment layer, free and unauthenticated, 492,021 segments, statewide extent, four-corner verified (Panhandle 55, East TX 449, Permian 199, South TX 36). Carries every field previously observed in _STATE.md (P5_NUM, OPER_NM is here as OPERATOR, SYS_NM as SYSTEM_NAME, COM_CARRIE as COMMODITY/COMMODITY_DESCRIPTION) plus DIAMETER, STATUS, SYSTEM_TYPE, INTERSTATE, T4PERMIT and — critically — COUNTY_FIPS and COUNTY_NAME already denormalised onto each segment, so county partitioning needs no spatial join. This is the RRC layer, NOT PHMSA NPMS, so the NPMS security restriction on precise alignment does not apply and the v1 ruling that NPMS is not needed holds. Use layer 13, not layer 12 (QPipelines): both return the identical 492,021 count and identical extent, so layer 12 is a generalised small-scale draw of the same data, and layer 13 is the full-resolution draw.

atomShapeNotes: R1 SPLIT RULE APPLIED: rrc-wells (point geometry, layer 1) and rrc-pipelines (line geometry, layer 13) are DIFFERENT SOURCE LAYERS with DIFFERENT GEOMETRY TYPES, so they SPLIT into two rails. This is correct as already manifested.

SUBCATEGORIZE, DO NOT SPLIT, on well status: producing-vs-plugged is an ATTRIBUTE of the same layer-1 point feature, so it stays inside the cell as an atom body field. Verified statewide attribute distribution via where-clause counts: Oil Well 316,298; Gas Well 126,429; Plugged Oil Well 331,856; Plugged Gas Well 68,160; Dry Hole 295,010; LIKE 'Plugged%' 423,477 total; LIKE '%Injection%' 41,975. 54 distinct GIS_SYMBOL_DESCRIPTION values exist statewide.

The existing atom body already has the right slots: buildPresentWellFactAtom in packages/engine-core/src/well-fact/well-fact-atoms.ts takes wellStatus, wellType, orphaned, surfaceLocation, parcelRelation, proximityRadiusMeters and proximityDistanceMeters. No contract change is required to adopt the statewide source — only the fetch and the field mapping change.

UPGRADE AVAILABLE: symnum.ts currently derives WellStatus and WellType from the numeric SYMNUM alone, with the docstring 'Public GIS carries SYMNUM only — not operator or regulatory status text.' That statement is TRUE OF THE HARRIS MIRROR AND FALSE OF THE RRC SOURCE. The RRC layer carries GIS_SYMBOL_DESCRIPTION as text ('Plugged Gas Well', 'Plugged Oil / Gas', 'Dry Hole', 'Shut-In Oil', 'Injection / Disposal', 'Water Supply Well', 'Core Test', ...). Prefer the authoritative text over the hand-maintained SYMNUM set-membership tables, and keep SYMNUM as a fallback. The current tables are demonstrably lossy: mapSymnumToWellStatus returns 'producing' as its default for any unmatched SYMNUM, which would mislabel statuses such as 'Canceled / Abandoned Location', 'Core Test' and 'Water Supply Well' as producing.

ORPHANED FLAG: derive by joining layer 2 (Orphan Wells, 11,937 features, fields OBJECTID/API/SHAPE only) on the API number, rather than inferring from SYMNUM. Layer 2 is the RRC's own orphan determination and is the authoritative answer to the orphaned question.

POSITIONAL CONFIDENCE: the RRC layer carries RELIAB (observed values '40', '15') and GIS_LOCATION_SOURCE (observed 'Operator reported location - Distances and Plat' and 'Commission`s hardcopy map'). These are a genuine confidence-and-provenance signal for the atom, satisfying the quality-gate rule better than an asserted number. A well positioned from a hardcopy map (RELIAB 15) should not carry the same confidence as an operator-plat location. Note the literal backtick in 'Commission`s hardcopy map' — it is in the source data; do not normalise silently.

NAMED BUFFER: the existing writer carries WELL_FACT_PROXIMITY_RADIUS_METERS = 152 in packages/engine-core/src/well-fact/plan-county-well-facts.ts, and that value flows into the atom body as proximityRadiusMeters so the adjacency claim is auditable. NOTE A DISCREPANCY: the dispatch names 152.4 m (exactly 500 ft) but the constant in source is the integer 152. 152 m is 498.69 ft, not 500 ft. Either the constant should become 152.4 or the '500 ft' framing in the docs should be corrected to '152 m'. Flagging rather than resolving — this is a doc-vs-code naming inconsistency, not a probe finding.

PIPELINE ATOM BODY: subcategorize within the rrc-pipelines cell on COMMODITY (natural gas 417,922 of 492,021), SYSTEM_TYPE ('Natural Gas Gathering' observed, note trailing whitespace padding in the raw value — trim it), STATUS ('In Service' 432,533 of 492,021), DIAMETER (inches, observed 10.75), INTERSTATE (Yes/No), and operator identity via OPERATOR + P5_NUM. T4PERMIT is the RRC permit number and is the natural citation key for a pipeline claim.

PIPELINE SEGMENTATION CAVEAT: one physical pipeline system appears as MANY rows. The East Texas sample returned three separate segments all sharing OPERATOR 'ENTERPRISE PRODUCTS OPERATINGLLC', SYSTEM_NAME 'FAIRPLAY', T4PERMIT '10680' and P5_NUM '253368', differing only by COUNTY_FIPS (183 GREGG, 401 RUSK, 183 GREGG again). A naive per-segment atom will emit duplicate-looking claims for the same pipeline crossing one parcel. Dedupe on T4PERMIT + P5_NUM when composing the parcel-level claim, and treat the segment as geometry rather than as identity.

OPERATOR NAME HYGIENE: observed 'ENTERPRISE PRODUCTS OPERATINGLLC' — the space before LLC is missing in the source. Operator strings are not clean; do not key identity on the name. P5_NUM is the RRC operator number and is the stable key.

stagingRecommendation.reasoning: PERSIST, do not live-fetch per writer run. The service caps every page at 1000 records (a resultRecordCount=2000 request returned exactly 1000 with exceededTransferLimit=true), so a full statewide pull is 1,397 sequential pages for wells and 493 for pipelines. Measured payloads at outFields=* with geometry are 451,767 bytes per 1000 wells (~452 B/feature) and 2,524,358 bytes per 1000 pipeline segments (~2.52 KB/feature), so a full pull moves roughly 0.63 GB of wells and 1.24 GB of pipelines. Re-streaming that on every county writer run is exactly the building-footprint anti-pattern that re-streams 394 MB per county and is the reason that rail is unusable. One statewide backfill into Postgres, refreshed on a cadence, costs roughly 0.49 GB for 1,396,049 well rows (point plus ~10 columns at ~350 B/row) and roughly 1.23 GB for 492,021 pipeline rows (linestring averaging ~2.5 KB), about 1.7 GB total before indexes; budget ~2.5 GB with a GiST spatial index on each. Two tables, not one, because the R1 split rule already separates them by geometry type. Naming follows the existing tx_special_district convention, which the special-district rail already stages successfully. Pipelines are cheap to partition because COUNTY_FIPS and COUNTY_NAME are already denormalised onto every segment — no spatial join needed for county slicing. Wells have no county column and must be assigned by point-in-county spatial join at load time; do that once at backfill, not per run. Prefer f=geojson (verified supported) with orderByFields=OBJECTID for stable pagination; the offset=500000 probe confirmed deep paging works.

blockers.blocker: Data vintage is UNKNOWN and not exposed by the service
blockers.evidence: Neither layer exposes editingInfo/lastEditDate, and copyrightText is empty on both the service and the layers. The RRC FAQ says only that the data 'is being continually updated and refined'. Atoms must therefore carry observedAt from the fetch timestamp and must NOT assert a source vintage. blockers.blocker: RRC's own accuracy disclaimer must not be laundered into an unqualified confidence signal
blockers.evidence: RRC FAQ verbatim: 'The data is intended solely for the internal use of the Railroad Commission, which makes no claim as to its accuracy or completeness.' Combined with per-record RELIAB values as low as 15 and GIS_LOCATION_SOURCE values such as 'Commission`s hardcopy map', a well location can be materially imprecise. A 152 m adjacency claim built on a hardcopy-map-derived point is weaker than the same claim on an operator-plat point, and the atom's confidence must reflect that rather than presenting a uniform number.

blockers.blocker: symnum.ts default-to-producing will mislabel wells at statewide scale
blockers.evidence: mapSymnumToWellStatus returns 'producing' for any SYMNUM not in its PLUGGED/DRY/PERMITTED sets. Statewide there are 54 distinct GIS_SYMBOL_DESCRIPTION values including 'Canceled / Abandoned Location', 'Core Test', 'Water Supply Well', 'Service' and 'Shut-In Oil'. On the 12,796-well Harris sample this was survivable; across 1,396,049 wells it becomes a large volume of wells asserted as producing that are not. Fix by preferring GIS_SYMBOL_DESCRIPTION text, which the new source provides and the old one did not.

blockers.blocker: Pipeline rows are per-county segments of the same permit, so naive atom emission duplicates claims
blockers.evidence: Three sampled East Texas segments shared T4PERMIT '10680', P5_NUM '253368', SYSTEM_NAME 'FAIRPLAY' and OPERATOR, differing only in COUNTY_FIPS (183/401/183). Dedupe on T4PERMIT+P5_NUM at claim composition.

adversarialFindings: I did not take the RRC service's statewide-ness on the strength of its extent alone. An extent is a bounding box and can be inflated by a handful of outlying features while the interior is empty. The four-corner probe is the real test, and both wells and pipelines returned non-zero in all four corners (wells 10/222/568/215, pipelines 55/449/199/36), plus a Dallas control at 2 wells. The counts also pattern-match Texas geology correctly: the Permian cell is the densest, the Panhandle cell is sparse, and East Texas is gas-heavy — a fake or partial layer would not reproduce that.

I initially reported the Harris mirror as returning empty for out-of-area probes, but that first attempt used a comma-string geometry parameter and the server returned nothing at all rather than a count — an ambiguous result I could have mistaken for a zero. I re-ran with a properly-formed JSON envelope and got the unambiguous pair: {"count":0} in the Permian and {"count":156} in a Houston control. Only the second run is evidence; the first was a malformed query.

CONTRADICTION FOUND AND RESOLVED: layers 12 (QPipelines) and 13 (Pipelines) return byte-identical counts (492,021) and identical extents. They are not two datasets to choose between — 12 is the generalised small-scale draw (minScale 1,000,000) and 13 the full-resolution draw (minScale 100,000). Recommending 13. Anyone treating them as independent sources would double-count.

The groupByFieldsForStatistics query returned 54 group labels with null counts — the server accepted the grouping but refused the count aggregate on the fields I tried. I did NOT report those nulls as zeros or infer a distribution from group ordering. I re-derived the real per-status counts with individual where-clause returnCountOnly queries, which is why the status figures in atomShapeNotes are each independently verified rather than read off one aggregate.

The 'no free bulk download' finding is a genuine negative result, not a search failure. I probed three plausible archive paths (all 404) and parsed the official data-sets page, which links only tabular well-record products and PDF manuals — no spatial archive. The FAQ's purchase framing corroborates. I am asserting absence here because the official page is the authoritative index, but I mark the underlying question — whether some unlinked archive exists — as UNKNOWN rather than proven-absent.

Every third-party alternative surfaced by the ArcGIS Online search is the same defect class as the bug that triggered this probe: New Fairview is one city, RRC_Wells_Coastal is the coastal zone by its own name, Denton County GIS is one county. I did not probe them further because recommending any of them would repeat the Harris mistake with a different bounding box. TxGIO does not hold RRC O&G layers at all — its service list is transportation-domain, so the dispatch's TxGIO hypothesis is disconfirmed.

The engine's own docstring in symnum.ts asserts 'Public GIS carries SYMNUM only — not operator or regulatory status text.' That is a false generalisation from the mirror to all public GIS, and it is the kind of claim that ossifies into an architectural constraint. The RRC source carries status text for wells and full operator identity for pipelines. Correcting the docstring matters as much as correcting the URL, or the next agent will re-derive the same limitation.

The dispatch's own '152.4 m / 500 ft' figure does not match the source constant, which is the integer 152 (= 498.69 ft). Small, but the entire point of a named buffer is that the adjacency claim is auditable, and an auditable claim cannot be off-by-a-foot between the doc and the code. Flagged, not silently fixed.

I am NOT asserting that the RRC service is licensed for commercial redistribution. It is public record and unauthenticated, and I found no ToS gate on the REST path, but the RRC's 'intended solely for the internal use of the Railroad Commission' disclaimer is unusual phrasing that a lawyer should read before this data is resold at Layer 2. Marking the commercial-redistribution question UNKNOWN rather than clearing it.

Scale reality check on the staging recommendation: at 1,396,049 wells and roughly 9 million Texas parcels, the well-fact rail will emit an absence atom for the overwhelming majority of parcels even with a correct source, because most Texas parcels genuinely have no well within 152 m. That is the honest answer and it is fine — but it means the rail's value concentrates in the Permian, East Texas and Eagle Ford, and a statewide completion percentage will look like near-total absence by design. Do not let that read as a coverage failure the way the zoning-stamp percentage once did.
